title: nginx HTTP/2 flow control and conditional module flaws corrupt worker memory
summary: HTTP/2 flow control can cause a heap overflow. F5 states that code execution also needs ASLR disabled or bypassed. The same releases fix use-after-free flaws in the resolver, HTTP/2, HTTP/3 and mail proxy.

severity.rationale: Network traffic can corrupt a reverse-proxy worker, but code execution requires defeating ASLR. HTTP/2 is common in developer and agent service front ends.

affected.note: First affected: flow control 1.9.5; resolver 0.6.18; HTTP/2 use-after-free 1.19.7; HTTP/3 1.25.0; mail proxy 0.5.33. Stable 1.30.7 and mainline 1.31.9 fix all five.

exposure: The corresponding HTTP/2, HTTP/3, resolver or mail proxy path must be used. For the HTTP/2 flow-control flaw, F5 identifies data-plane exposure and an ASLR prerequisite for code execution. NGINX Plus needs its own fix mapping.

params.instructions: Check nginx Open Source version, affected release line and the documented exposure conditions.

remediation.action: Update or contain the affected component
remediation.details: Upgrade to nginx 1.30.7 or 1.31.9 on the corresponding line, or a vendor build carrying the fix, and restart workers.
remediation.risk: Medium. Updates can interrupt workflows and require compatibility checks.

verification: Confirm the deployed release meets the corresponding fixed version and verify the affected workflow with harmless test inputs.

review.notes: Independent reviewer re-read every tier 1 source and checked every field. No open findings.

history.change: Initial record drafted from directly inspected primary sources for independent review.
